Year-over-year (and period-over-period) change

Source: R/yoy.R, R/yoy_output.R
yoy.Rd

Computes the change from one period to the period lag places before it, matched on the period's own value rather than on row order, and carries an exact interval for count data. Use it for the “up 12% on last year” figures of an annual report or an open-data release: a missing year shows as a gap instead of shifting every comparison, a percentage is compared in percentage points, and a change off a small count comes with an interval as wide as the count is small.

Usage

yoy(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
yoy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
yoy(
  x,
  value,
  prd,
  by = NULL,
  lag = 1L,
  fun = NULL,
  units = c("count", "continuous", "percent"),
  minbase = NULL,
  conflvl = 0.95,
  dir = c("neutral", "higher", "lower"),
  complete = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'numeric'
yoy(x, prd = seq_along(x), ...)

# S3 method for class 'integer'
yoy(x, prd = seq_along(x), ...)

# S3 method for class 'ts'
yoy(x, lag = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'rmbl_yoy'
print(x, digits = 1L, palette = "diverging", color = NULL, n = 30, ...)

Arguments

x

An rmbl_yoy object returned by yoy().

...

Ignored.

value

For a data frame, the column holding the measure, as a string or a bare name.

prd

For a data frame, the column holding the period (a year, a Date, a fiscal-year integer, an ordered factor). An ordered factor is compared by level order, one level being one period; an unordered factor or a character column has no order, so every row is flagged “no comparison period”. For a numeric vector, the periods themselves.

by

Optional grouping columns, as a character vector. The change is computed within each group.

lag

How many periods back to compare with. 1 is year-over-year on annual data; for a ts the default follows the series' own frequency, so monthly data compares with the same month a year earlier.

fun

How several rows of one period (and group) are combined into one value: NULL (the default) sums counts (sum()) and averages continuous values and percentages (mean()); pass a function of a numeric vector returning one number to choose.

units

What the measure is. "count" gets the exact rate-ratio interval. "continuous" gets the percent change without one, since a single pair of totals carries no information about its own variability. "percent" reports a percentage-POINT change and withholds the percent change, which for a percentage is a different quantity.

minbase

Optional: previous-period values below this get a “small base” note. Nothing is withheld either way: every non-zero base gets its percent change and exact interval, which is as wide as the base is small. Defaults to 0 (no note); only a zero base has no percent change.

conflvl

Numeric scalar in (0, 1), the confidence level for the count interval; default 0.95.

dir

Which way is an improvement: "higher", "lower" (segregation days, deaths in custody, use of force), or "neutral". Affects colour and the verdict column only, never the arithmetic.

complete

Logical scalar, default TRUE: insert the missing periods in the observed range so that a gap is visible as a gap instead of closing up.

digits

Integer, default 1. Decimal places shown in the percent (or percentage-point) change column. The interval column is always shown to whole percent.

palette

Character, default "diverging". One of yoypals(); chooses the colours used when color = TRUE. An unknown name is an error.

color

Logical or NULL (the default). TRUE wraps each row in 24-bit ANSI colour codes chosen from its verdict; FALSE prints plain text. NULL means colour only in an interactive session with the NO_COLOR environment variable unset, so output that is redirected or captured stays plain text.

n

Integer, default 30. Maximum number of rows printed; the number of rows left out is reported on a final line.

Value

An rmbl_yoy object (a data frame of class c("rmbl_yoy", "data.frame")) with one row per period (and group): the period column under its own name (period for a vector or a ts), the grouping columns, then value, previous, change, pctchg (or ppchg for percentages), flag (character: “no comparison period”, “no data”, “previous period is zero”, or a small-base note when minbase is set; NA otherwise), pctlo and pctup for counts, and verdict. Attribute "yoy" records value, period, by, lag, units, minbase, conflvl, direction and the display digits; the writers (yoywr()) and yoysmry() read it.

Details

Rows are first combined to one per period (and group) with fun. With complete = TRUE the periods missing from a regular grid (numbers, Date or POSIXct with a common step) are inserted with NA values and flagged “no data”. Each period is then compared with the period lag steps earlier in that grid: change is the difference, pctchg \(100 (v_t / v_{t-lag} - 1)\) (NA off a zero base), and for percentages ppchg is the difference in percentage points.

For counts, conditional on their sum \(n = a + b\) the current count \(a\) is binomial with probability \(\rho / (1 + \rho)\), \(\rho\) the rate ratio; the Clopper-Pearson interval for that probability, transformed back, is an exact interval for the ratio, reported as pctlo and pctup (percent change). It is the interval stats::poisson.test() gives for two counts with equal exposure. A zero base has no percent change but still an interval (with an infinite upper end).

verdict is "up", "down" or "unchanged" for direction = "neutral", and "better", "worse" or "unchanged" otherwise; it reads the sign of the change only and makes no claim of significance.

Errors: x neither a data frame, a numeric vector nor a ts; value, period or by naming a column that does not exist; a non-numeric or infinite value; for units = "count", negative or fractional values; lag not a positive whole number; conflvl outside (0, 1); an unknown units or direction.

0.5.x argument names

The 0.5.x names period, min_base, conf_level and direction are still accepted for prd, minbase, conflvl and dir, the names to use, as are the 0.5.x values "higher_is_better" and "lower_is_better" of dir. A call that gives both names of one argument is refused.

References

The exact interval for a ratio of two counts is the conditional-binomial (Clopper-Pearson) one, which is the construction stats::poisson.test uses and which this is verified against. On the reporting conventions, the Toronto Police Service's Understanding Strip Searches in 2020 Methodological Report – in the local corpus – reports year-over-year change on exactly this kind of administrative extract, and is the shape this function is built for.

See also

yoyhtml(), yoypdf(), yoysmry()

Examples

seg <- data.frame(
  EndFiscalYear = rep(2019:2023, each = 2),
  Gender = rep(c("Female", "Male"), 5),
  NumberOfPlacements = c(31, 402, 28, 377, 12, 190, 19, 268, 24, 331)
)

y <- yoy(seg,
  value = "NumberOfPlacements", prd = "EndFiscalYear",
  by = "Gender", dir = "lower"
)
y
#> Gender  EndFiscalYear  NumberOfPlacements  previous  change  change %  interval     
#> ──────  ─────────────  ──────────────────  ────────  ──────  ────────  ─────────────
#> Female  2019           31                  —         —         —       —            
#>     ↳ note: no comparison period
#> Female  2020           28                  31        -3      ▼ -9.7%   [-48%, +56%] 
#> Female  2021           12                  28        -16     ▼ -57.1%  [-80%, -13%] 
#> Female  2022           19                  12        7       ▲ +58.3%  [-27%, +258%]
#> Female  2023           24                  19        5       ▲ +26.3%  [-34%, +144%]
#> Male    2019           402                 —         —         —       —            
#>     ↳ note: no comparison period
#> Male    2020           377                 402       -25     ▼ -6.2%   [-19%, +8%]  
#> Male    2021           190                 377       -187    ▼ -49.6%  [-58%, -40%] 
#> Male    2022           268                 190       78      ▲ +41.1%  [+17%, +71%] 
#> Male    2023           331                 268       63      ▲ +23.5%  [+5%, +46%]  
#> 
#> lag 1 period · units: count · 95% exact rate-ratio interval · lower is better

# The interval is exact, so a small group does not get a confident
# percent it has not earned.
subset(as.data.frame(y), Gender == "Female")
#>   Gender EndFiscalYear value previous change     pctchg                 flag
#> 1 Female          2019    31       NA     NA         NA no comparison period
#> 2 Female          2020    28       31     -3  -9.677419                 <NA>
#> 3 Female          2021    12       28    -16 -57.142857                 <NA>
#> 4 Female          2022    19       12      7  58.333333                 <NA>
#> 5 Female          2023    24       19      5  26.315789                 <NA>
#>       pctlo     pctup verdict
#> 1        NA        NA    <NA>
#> 2 -47.79679  55.62836  better
#> 3 -80.14950 -12.97354  better
#> 4 -27.02865 257.66674   worse
#> 5 -33.67876 143.90121   worse

# A percentage is handled as percentage points, not as a percent of a
# percent.
rate <- data.frame(year = 2019:2023, share = c(4.1, 4.6, 5.2, 5.0, 5.4))
yoy(rate, value = "share", prd = "year", units = "percent")
#> year  share  previous  change  points  
#> ────  ─────  ────────  ──────  ────────
#> 2019  4.1    —         —         —     
#>     ↳ note: no comparison period
#> 2020  4.6    4.1       0.5     ▲ +0.5pp
#> 2021  5.2    4.6       0.6     ▲ +0.6pp
#> 2022  5.0    5.2       -0.2    ▼ -0.2pp
#> 2023  5.4    5.0       0.4     ▲ +0.4pp
#> 
#> lag 1 period · units: percent · percentage-point change, not percent of a percent

# a missing year stays a gap; a bare column name works too
yoy(data.frame(year = c(2019, 2021, 2022), n = c(10, 12, 15)), value = n, prd = year)
#> year  n   previous  change  change %  interval     
#> ────  ──  ────────  ──────  ────────  ─────────────
#> 2019  10  —         —         —       —            
#>     ↳ note: no comparison period
#> 2020  —   10        —         —       —            
#>     ↳ note: no data
#> 2021  12  —         —         —       —            
#>     ↳ note: no comparison period
#> 2022  15  12        3       ▲ +25.0%  [-45%, +192%]
#> 
#> lag 1 period · units: count · 95% exact rate-ratio interval

# a quarterly series compares each quarter with the same quarter a year earlier
q <- ts(c(5, 6, 7, 8, 6, 7, 9, 9), frequency = 4, start = c(2020, 1))
as.data.frame(yoy(q))[5:8, c("period", "value", "previous", "pctchg")]
#>    period value previous   pctchg
#> 5 2021.00     6        5 20.00000
#> 6 2021.25     7        6 16.66667
#> 7 2021.50     9        7 28.57143
#> 8 2021.75     9        8 12.50000

# counts must be whole numbers
try(yoy(data.frame(year = 1:3, n = c(1.5, 2, 3)), "n", "year"))
#> Error : `units = "count"` needs non-negative whole numbers; use units = "continuous" for a measured quantity
